metadata.name: Diabetes mellitus (Type 2)
metadata.emergency_level: Routine (chronic) — but DKA and hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS) are emergencies
metadata.severity: Ranges from diet-controlled to complicated with end-organ damage; acute hyperglycaemic crises are life-threatening

overview.short_description: A chronic metabolic disorder of insulin resistance with relative insulin deficiency causing hyperglycaemia; usually adult-onset, strongly linked to obesity and inactivity, and a major cause of cardiovascular, renal, retinal and neurological disease.
overview.detailed_description: Type 2 diabetes accounts for ~90% of diabetes. It develops when peripheral insulin resistance is no longer compensated by pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion, producing chronic hyperglycaemia. It is frequently preceded by years of prediabetes and is often asymptomatic at diagnosis, detected on screening. Long-term hyperglycaemia drives microvascular (retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy) and macrovascular (coronary, cerebrovascular, peripheral arterial) complications. Management is multifactorial: glycaemia, blood pressure, lipids, weight, and cardiovascular/renal protection.
overview.pathophysiology: Core defects: (1) insulin resistance in muscle, liver and adipose tissue; (2) progressive beta-cell dysfunction/failure; (3) increased hepatic glucose output; plus incretin deficiency, increased glucagon, renal glucose reabsorption, and adipose lipolysis (the 'ominous octet'). Chronic hyperglycaemia causes advanced glycation, oxidative stress and microvascular damage.
overview.etiology: Polygenic predisposition combined with obesity (especially visceral), physical inactivity, high-calorie diet, ageing, and ethnicity (higher risk in South Asian, MENA, African, Hispanic populations). Secondary/other forms: pancreatic disease, steroid-induced, endocrinopathies (Cushing, acromegaly), monogenic (MODY), gestational.
overview.incubation_period: Not applicable; prediabetes may precede diagnosis by years.
overview.natural_history: Gradual progression from insulin resistance/prediabetes to overt diabetes; beta-cell function declines over time so many patients eventually need intensifying therapy including insulin. Good early control reduces long-term complications ('legacy effect').
overview.prognosis: Good with early, sustained multifactorial control; substantial excess cardiovascular and renal risk if poorly controlled. Remission is possible in some with major weight loss early in disease.

prevalence.value: ~10% of adults globally and rising; higher in MENA/North Africa. IDF estimates >500 million adults with diabetes worldwide.

incidence.value: Rising with obesity epidemic; increasing onset in younger adults and adolescents.

mortality.value: Major cause of premature death, chiefly via cardiovascular disease and renal failure.

epidemiology.age_groups: Typically >40 but increasingly in younger adults; prediabetes very common in mid-life.
epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; especially high burden in MENA, South Asia, Pacific Islands.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Physical inactivity, energy-dense diet, sugary drinks, poor sleep.
risk_factors.smoking: Increases insulin resistance and cardiovascular/renal complication risk.
risk_factors.alcohol: Excess contributes to weight gain and can cause hypo/hyperglycaemia; moderation advised.
risk_factors.obesity: Strongest modifiable risk factor, especially central/visceral adiposity.
risk_factors.hypertension: Commonly coexists (metabolic syndrome); compounds cardiovascular/renal risk.
risk_factors.pregnancy: Prior gestational diabetes markedly raises future T2DM risk; PCOS also associated.
risk_factors.family_history: Strong; first-degree relative substantially increases risk.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Polygenic; monogenic MODY in a minority (young, lean, strong family history).
risk_factors.medications: Corticosteroids, some antipsychotics, thiazides (high dose), protease inhibitors can precipitate/unmask diabetes.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Prediabetes, gestational diabetes, PCOS, pancreatitis, hypertension, dyslipidaemia.

chief_complaints.importance: Many T2DM diagnosed on screening while asymptomatic

chief_complaints.complaint: Recurrent infections (thrush, skin, UTI) or slow-healing wounds

symptoms.importance: Red flag for insulin deficiency (consider T1DM)
Often the presenting clue in primary care

negative_findings.why_important: Common in early T2DM — absence does NOT exclude; diagnosis is biochemical

negative_findings.finding: No ketones / not acidotic / not dehydrated
negative_findings.why_important: Makes DKA/HHS unlikely — supports routine outpatient management

history_questions.question: Any increased thirst, urination, weight loss, fatigue, or recurrent thrush/infections?
history_questions.why_ask: Classic hyperglycaemic symptoms and presenting clues

history_questions.question: Family history of diabetes; personal history of gestational diabetes or PCOS?
Any numbness/tingling in feet, visual change, chest pain, or foot ulcers?
history_questions.why_ask: Screens for existing complications at diagnosis

history_questions.question: Medications such as steroids or antipsychotics?
Rapid onset, marked weight loss, young/lean, or ketosis?
history_questions.why_ask: Suggests Type 1 or ketosis-prone diabetes needing insulin urgently

physical_examination.examination: Foot examination (pulses, sensation with 10 g monofilament, skin/ulcers, deformity)

physical_examination.expected_finding: Diabetic retinopathy may already be present

physical_examination.examination: Hydration status / conscious level (if acutely unwell)

vital_signs.blood_pressure: Often elevated (comorbid hypertension); low in HHS with dehydration

laboratory_tests.expected_result: >=48 mmol/mol (6.5%) diagnostic on two occasions if asymptomatic
Random >=11.1 with symptoms diagnostic; 2-h OGTT >=11.1 diagnostic

laboratory_tests.test_name: Lipid profile, U&E/eGFR, urine ACR, LFTs

laboratory_tests.indication: If unwell, marked hyperglycaemia, or suspected T1DM/DKA

imaging.when_needed: Suspected peripheral arterial disease or foot complications

ecg.findings: May show silent ischaemia, prior infarction, LVH.

other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: Not applicable (consider C-peptide and islet autoantibodies to distinguish T1 vs T2 if uncertain)

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: WHO/ADA: HbA1c >=48 mmol/mol (6.5%), OR fasting plasma glucose >=7.0 mmol/L, OR 2-h OGTT glucose >=11.1 mmol/L, OR random glucose >=11.1 mmol/L with classic symptoms. In the absence of unequivocal hyperglycaemia, confirm with a repeat test.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: Risk scores (e.g., FINDRISC, QDiabetes) identify high-risk individuals for screening; not diagnostic.

cutoff_values.value: HbA1c: <42 normal, 42-47 prediabetes, >=48 mmol/mol diabetes. FPG: <5.6 normal, 5.6-6.9 IFG, >=7.0 diabetes. 2-h OGTT: <7.8 normal, 7.8-11.0 IGT, >=11.1 diabetes (mmol/L).

differential_diagnosis.differences: Younger/leaner, rapid onset, marked weight loss, ketosis, insulin-deficient
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_labs: Positive islet autoantibodies (GAD), low C-peptide, ketones
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: How quickly did symptoms develop? Weight loss? Ketones?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Acute, unwell, dehydrated, acidotic (DKA) or profoundly hyperosmolar (HHS)

differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Steroid use? Pancreatic disease? Young lean strong family history?

differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Very large volumes of dilute urine
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is your blood sugar normal despite thirst?

diagnostic_questions.question: How quickly did the thirst/weight loss develop, and are you passing ketones or feeling very unwell?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Rapid onset + weight loss + ketones -> urgent insulin/T1

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you take steroids or antipsychotics?

next_best_question.question: Can we repeat the HbA1c to confirm before diagnosis?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Confirmed -> diagnose and stage; borderline -> prediabetes pathway and lifestyle

next_best_question.question: Do you have vomiting, drowsiness, or deep rapid breathing?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Yes -> urgent assessment for DKA/HHS; No -> start outpatient management

next_best_test.why: Establish diagnosis (repeat unless unequivocal symptomatic hyperglycaemia)

next_best_test.test: Baseline complications screen (ACR, eGFR, lipids, retinal, foot exam)

red_flags.finding: Marked hyperglycaemia with vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsiness, deep breathing, ketones
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency — assess/treat DKA (IV fluids, insulin, potassium) in hospital

red_flags.finding: Very high glucose with severe dehydration and confusion in older adult
red_flags.immediate_action: Emergency — hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state; urgent admission

red_flags.finding: Diabetic foot with spreading infection, deep ulcer, or critical ischaemia
red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent same-day multidisciplinary foot service / admission

red_flags.finding: Rapid weight loss with ketosis in a lean patient
red_flags.immediate_action: Urgent — likely Type 1; do not delay insulin

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Suspected Type 1/ketosis-prone diabetes, pregnancy with diabetes, suspected DKA/HHS (emergency), acute diabetic foot.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Poor control despite optimisation, suspected MODY/secondary cause, complex comorbidity, complications needing specialist care (nephrology, ophthalmology, podiatry).
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: DKA, HHS, severe hypoglycaemia not responding, limb-threatening foot sepsis/ischaemia.

initial_management.supportive_care: Structured education, dietary and physical-activity support, smoking cessation, individualised HbA1c target (often ~48-58 mmol/mol / 6.5-7.5%). Address all cardiovascular risk factors, not glucose alone.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Modified-release metformin; SGLT-2 inhibitor; GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide; Insulin or hypoglycaemia-causing agent. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG28_2026.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Weight loss (5-10%+ can markedly improve control; early substantial weight loss can induce remission in some), reduced refined carbohydrate/sugary drinks, Mediterranean-style diet, regular activity, alcohol moderation, smoking cessation.
initial_management.follow_up: HbA1c every 3-6 months until stable then 6-monthly; annual review of renal function (eGFR/ACR), lipids, BP, feet, and retinal screening; medication review and hypoglycaemia/sick-day education.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Metformin first-line (unless contraindicated). Add agents with proven cardiovascular/renal benefit early, especially SGLT2 inhibitors and/or GLP-1 receptor agonists in those with established/high cardiovascular risk, heart failure, or CKD. Other options: DPP-4 inhibitors, sulfonylureas, pioglitazone, insulin when needed. Statin for cardiovascular risk; manage BP; consider antiplatelet in secondary prevention.

patient_education.home_advice: Diabetes is a long-term condition you can manage well: eat healthily and cut sugary drinks, stay active, lose excess weight, take your medicines, check and protect your feet daily, attend eye and kidney checks, and don't smoke.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: السكري حالة مزمنة يمكن التحكم بها جيداً: تناول طعاماً صحياً وقلّل المشروبات السكرية، وحافظ على النشاط وأنقِص الوزن الزائد، وتناول أدويتك، وافحص قدميك واعتنِ بهما يومياً، والتزم بفحوصات العين والكلى، ولا تدخّن.
patient_education.prevention: For prediabetes/high risk: weight loss, activity, healthy diet reduce progression; metformin in selected high-risk people.
patient_education.warning_signs: Seek urgent care for vomiting with high sugars, drowsiness, deep/rapid breathing, severe dehydration, a foot ulcer/spreading redness, or repeated hypoglycaemia.

prevention.vaccination: Recommend annual influenza and pneumococcal (and other indicated) vaccines given higher infection risk.
prevention.lifestyle: Weight management, physical activity, healthy diet, no smoking — primary prevention in at-risk individuals.
prevention.screening: Screen high-risk adults (obesity, family history, prior GDM, high-risk ethnicity, hypertension) with HbA1c/fasting glucose; identify and manage prediabetes.

evidence.evidence_level: High — large RCTs and cardiovascular/renal outcome trials (UKPDS, EMPA-REG, LEADER, CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD, etc.).
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG28_2026; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
evidence.legacy_guideline_strength_pre_v13: Strong — ADA/EASD consensus, NICE NG28, WHO.

treatment_guidance.treatment_goal: Individualise glucose treatment while prioritising cardiovascular/renal protection and avoiding hypoglycaemia/DKA.
treatment_guidance.legacy_narrative_summary: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Modified-release metformin; SGLT-2 inhibitor; GLP-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide; Insulin or hypoglycaemia-causing agent. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG28_2026.

pregnancy or breastfeeding status when relevant
documented drug allergies and the exact reaction
all prescribed, OTC, herbal and recreational substances
major cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and bleeding history
non_drug_measures: Structured education, nutrition/activity support, foot care, smoking cessation and eye/renal/cardiovascular risk management.

medication_options.when_to_consider: After eGFR, tolerance and comorbidity review
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: severe renal impairment below the licensed threshold or acute metabolic acidosis
use_caution_if: acute illness/dehydration, hypoxia, liver failure, heavy alcohol use, contrast studies, or vitamin B12 deficiency
monitoring: eGFR, gastrointestinal tolerance, HbA1c and periodic B12 in at-risk patients

medication_options.when_to_consider: Current NICE pathway based on comorbidity and eligibility
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: active diabetic ketoacidosis or inability to follow sick-day rules
use_caution_if: recurrent genital infection, volume depletion, low carbohydrate intake, frailty, CKD, pregnancy, or planned surgery
monitoring: renal function, volume status, genital/urinary symptoms; ketones when unwell; temporary withholding during acute illness/fasting/surgery

medication_options.when_to_consider: When eligibility and patient factors support it
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

use_caution_if: prior pancreatitis, severe gastroparesis, gallbladder disease, dehydration risk, or concurrent insulin/sulfonylurea
monitoring: weight, glucose, gastrointestinal tolerance, hydration and symptoms of pancreatitis/gallbladder disease

medication_options.when_to_consider: Symptomatic/severe hyperglycaemia or inadequate control under clinician supervision
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: no absolute disease-wide exclusion when insulin is urgently required; selection must be clinician-directed
use_caution_if: recurrent hypoglycaemia, renal/hepatic impairment, frailty, irregular meals, driving, cognitive impairment, or concomitant glucose-lowering medicines
monitoring: glucose/HbA1c, hypoglycaemia, weight, injection technique and sick-day management

medication_options.clinical_note: Must include hypoglycaemia education, driving advice, dose individualisation and monitoring.

procedures_referral_and_escalation: Urgent care for ketones/acidosis, hyperosmolar state, severe hypoglycaemia, pregnancy with uncontrolled glucose or acute diabetic foot.
